Weather summary 
As per weather forecast received from Meteorological C entre, Ahmedabad probability of 
cloudy sky during next five days  with light rainfall on 12-09-2026, 13-09-2026,               
16-09-2026; moderate rainfall on 1 4-09-2026 and 15 -09-2026 at isolated places very 
likely. Extended Range Forecast : Maximum temperature, minimum temperature  likely 
to be normal and rainfall likely to be below normal during subsequent week 16-09-2026 
to 22-09-2026 in Gujarat region. 
Note: The above given weather forecast is average situation for whole district, so it should not  applicable 
for one place.

2 | P a g e  
 
Advisory 
General 
advice 
Undertake interculturing and weeding operations to conserve moisture in 
standing monsoon crops and apply need based light irrigation by considering 
weather and soil moisture condition in standing crops. Application of 
fertilizer or top dressing  should undertake onl y under optimum soil 
moisture condition in standing crops. Farmers are advised to download 
MEGHDOOT mobile application for acquiring information regarding Agromet 
Advisory in Gujarati  language. Click on following link to download this 
application user: 
https://play,google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.aas.meghdoot 
Field Crops Stage Advisory 
Rice 
Booting/ 
Heading/ 
Flowering 
 Maintain 5-7 cm stagnant water in rice field. 
 Spray mixture of streptocycline 1 g + copper 
oxychloride 20 g fungicides in 400 -500 litres of water 
per hectare to control bacterial leaf blight disease. 
 Spray tricyclazole 75 WP 6 g or Iprobenfos 48 EC 10 ml 
in 10 litres of water at an interval of 15 to 2 0 days to 
control blast disease. 
 For proper nutrient mana gement in transplanted rice,  
first top dressing of nitrogen fertilizer should be 
applied 30 –40 days after transplanting. Apply 32 kg of 
nitrogen per hectare for early -maturing varieties, 40 kg 
of nit rogen per hectare for medium to l ate-maturing 
varieties and 48 kg of nitrogen per hectare for late -
maturing varieties. 
 The rice yellow stem borer in rice can be effectively 
managed by installing five pheromone traps per hectare 
baited with lures that attra ct the male moths. Spray 
neem-based insecticides by mixing 10 ml (5 EC) to 60 ml 
(0.03 EC) in 10 litres of water. Alternatively, apply 
Cartap Hydrochloride 4 G @ 8 kg per acre or Fipronil 
0.3G with  10 kg  per acre or Chlorantraniliprole 0.4G 
with 4 kg per acre after reducing the water level in the 
field. These granular insecticides should be applied 
twice, first application at the onset of pest infestation or 
30–35 days after transplanting and  second application 
at 15–20 days later. This schedule helps keep  the pest 
infestation under control.

3 | P a g e  
 
Cotton 
Squaring/ 
Flowering/ 
Boll formation 
 If irrigation facilities are available then apply need 
based irrigation through drip irrigation/alternate 
furrow irrigation method by considering soil moisture 
condition in standing crop. 
 Avoid application of fertilizers during long dry spell 
condition or it should apply under optimum soil 
moisture condition. Spray 2 % urea during dry spell in 
standing cotton crop. 
 Sucking pest infestation in cotton  at initial stage can be 
controlled by  spraying 500 g of neem seed kernel 
extract (5% NSKE) or 50 ml of neem oil or a neem-based 
insecticide by mixing 10 ml (5 EC) to 50 ml (0.03 EC) in 
10 litres of water. If the infestation is severe, spray 
Flonicamid 50 WG with 3 g or Diafenthiuron 50 WP with 
10 g or Dinotefuran 20 SG with 3 g by mixing the 
recommended quantity in 10 litres of water. 
 To prevent an increase in the population of whiteflies 
and jassids (leafhoppers), do not use synthetic 
pyrethroid insecticides until the month of November. 
Groundnut Flowering/ 
Pod formation 
 Leaf-eating caterpillar (Spodoptera) in groundnut can 
be controlled by installing one light trap per hectare in 
the affected area and destroy the adult moths and leaf -
eating caterpillar moths attracted to the trap. 
 White grubs in groundnut can be controlled by spraying 
Chlorpyrifos 20 EC with 4 litres per hectare through 
drip irrigation or along with irrigation. If irrigation is 
not being given but intermittent rainfall is occurring, 
prepare the insecticide solution in a spray pump, 
remove the nozzle and apply the solution directly into 
the furrows in the required quantity. 
 Leaf-eating caterpillar (Spodoptera) in groundnut can 
be controlled by installing pheromone traps with 40 
traps per hectare on a community basis to keep the pest 
population under control. At the initial stage of 
infestation, spray either neem seed kernel powder 
extract at 500 g (5% extract) or a neem -based 
insecticide at 20 ml (1 EC) to 40 ml (0.15 EC) mixed in 
10 litres  of water. If the infestation becomes severe, 
spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC at 3 ml or 
Flubendiamide 20 WG at 6 g or Thiamethoxam 12.6% + 
Lambda-cyhalothrin 9.5% ZC at 3 ml 10 litres of water.

4 | P a g e  
 
 Cutworms in groundnut can be controlled by installing 
one l ight trap per hectare to attract and destroy the 
moths. Prepare a 5% neem extract by mixing 500 g of 
neem seed kernel powder or neem leaves in 10 litres of 
water and spray it on the crop. If the infestation is 
severe, spray either Indoxacarb 14.5 SC with 1 0 ml per 
10 litres of water or Emamectin benzoate 5 SG with 5 g 
per 10 litres of water. 
Green 
gram 
Flowering/ 
Pod formation 
 Apply need based light irrigation by considering 
weather and soil moisture condition in green gram 
crop. 
 Mosaic of leaf curl disease is transmitted due to white 
fly so to control it, spray imidacloprid 17.8 SC 3 ml or 
acetamiprid 20 SP 2 g or azadirachtin 40 ml in 10 litres 
of water in green gram crop.  
 Hairy caterpillar in green gram can be controlled by 
installing one light trap per hectare to attract and 
destroy the adult moths of.  Spray 500 g of neem seed 
kernel powder or neem leaves (5% extract) mixed in 10 
litres of water to control hairy caterpillar in clear and 
calm weather condition.  If the infestation is severe, 
spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC with 4 ml or 
Indoxacarb 15.8 EC with 6 ml or Emamectin Benzoate 5 
SG with 5 g mixed in 10 litres of water.  
 The infestation by aphids, whiteflies, leafhoppers and 
thrips in green gram at initial stage can be controlled by 
spraying 500 g of neem seed kernel powder (5% 
extract) or 40 g of the fungal biocontrol agent 
Verticillium lecanii powder mixed in 10 litres of water. 
 If there is a severe infestation of aphids in green gram 
and predatory inse cts are absent, spray Imidacloprid 
17.8 SL with 2.5 ml or Thiamethoxam 25 WG with 4 g 
per 10 litres of water. 
Black gram Flowering/ 
Pod formation 
 Apply need based light irrigation by considering 
weather and soil moisture condition in black gram crop. 
 Mosaic of leaf curl disease is transmitted due to white 
fly so to control it, spray imidacloprid 17.8 SC 3 ml or 
acetamiprid 20 SP 2 g or azadirachtin 40 ml in 10 litres 
of water in green gram crop.

5 | P a g e  
 
 Hairy caterpillar in black gram can be controlled by 
installing one light trap per hectare to attract and 
destroy the adult moths.  Spray 500 g of neem seed 
kernel powder or neem leaves (5% extract) mixed in 10 
litres of water to control hairy caterpillar in clear and 
calm weather condition.  If the infestation i s severe, 
spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC with 4 ml or 
Indoxacarb 15.8 EC with 6 ml or Emamectin Benzoate 5 
SG with 5 g, mixed in 10 litres of water.  
 The infestation by aphids, whiteflies, leafhoppers and 
thrips in black gram at initial stage can be controlled by 
spraying 500 g of neem seed kernel powder (5% 
extract) or 40 g of the fungal biocontrol agent 
Verticillium lecanii powder mixed in 10 litres of water. 
 If there is a severe infestation of aphids in black gram 
and predatory insects are absent, spray either 
Imidacloprid 17.8 SL with 2.5 ml per 10 litres of water 
or Thiamethoxam 25 WG with 4 g per 10 litres of water. 
Pigeon pea Vegetative 
 Apply need based light irrigation by considering 
weather and soil moisture condition in pigeon pea crop. 
 Perform hand weeding three times at 40 and 60 days 
after sowing. 
Pearl millet Heading/ 
Flowering 
 Shoot fly  in pearl millet can be controlled by  removing 
and destroy ing plants damaged by the pest during the 
early crop stage. At the initial stage of infestat ion, spray 
Beauveria bassiana 1.15% WP at 40 g mixed in 10 litres 
of water in clear and calm weather condition . In case of 
severe infestation, spray either Quinalphos 25 EC at 20 
ml or Cypermethrin 10 EC at 5 ml  mixed in 10 litres of 
water. 
 Downy mildew in  pearl millet  can be controlled by 
spraying Metalaxyl-MZ 72 WP with 15 g per 10 litres of 
water, as required, ensuring thorough coverage of both 
the upper and lower surfaces of the leaves. 
Fruit Crop Stage Advisory 
Chilli Vegetative 
 Apply need based light irrigation by considering 
weather and soil moisture condition in chilli crop. 
 Thrips in chilli can be controlled by s praying neem seed 
oil 30 to 50 ml in 10 lit res. In case of heavy attack, spray 
of spinosad 45 SC 3 ml or spinetoram 11.7 SC 10 ml in 
10 litres of water.

6 | P a g e  
 
Tomato Vegetative 
 Apply need based light irrigation by considering 
weather and soil moisture condition in tomato crop. 
 Pinworm at initial incidence in tomato can be 
controlled by  installing 40 yellow sticky traps per 
hectare. In heavy incidence, spray Chlorantraniliprole 
18.5 SC 3 ml or Flubendiamide 480 SC 3 ml in 10 litres 
of water. 
Brinjal Vegetative 
 Apply need based light irrigation by considering 
weather and soil moisture condition in brinjal crop 
 Sucking pest like white fly and jassid in brinjal can be 
controlled by s praying Difenthiuron 50 WP 4 ml or 
Thiamethoxam 25 WG 4 g in 10 litres of water.  
Livestock 
 Keep animals at safer places in shed during abnormal weather condition.  
 Spray phenyl in the animal shed to avoid files and mosquitoes.   
 Don’t allow your animals to congregate under trees.   
 Vaccinate the animals against outbreaks of diseases like Foot & Mouth disease (FMD), 
Haemorrhagic Septicaemia (H.S.) and Black quarter (B.Q.) during onset of monsoon. 
Note: Advisories are prepared based on medium range weather forecast received from 
Meteorological Centre, Ahmedabad.
